findings.issue_text: The `canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles` methods in `ClientPermissionsV2` drop the admin-role short-circuit check (`root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)` directly or via `canManage`/`canView`) that every sibling method (`canManage`, `canView`, `canConfigure`) performs, consulting only the FGAP resource store; as a result, in any deployment with the V2 feature enabled, an admin holding `manage-clients` — including the master/realm admin — gets 403 when mapping that client's roles to a user, adding composites to its roles, or managing its client-scope role mappings, unless an explicit FGAP permission is also created. The PR's tests only exercise a role-less user (`myadmin`) so they cannot catch this, and the javadoc omission on these methods suggests the behavior may be deliberate — intent should be confirmed.

In `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)`, the 'all-clients' type-level fallback only fires when no per-client resource exists; once a per-client resource exists, evaluation runs only against that resource and the type-level resource is never consulted. Since deleting a scope permission (the standard authz admin API, used in the tests' `@AfterEach`) removes the policy but not the resource, an orphaned policy-less per-client resource permanently shadows type-level grants: after deleting a client-specific permission and later granting an 'all clients' MANAGE permission, that one client returns 403 forever. The same shadowing occurs with a live per-client resource holding a grant for a different scope (e.g., per-client VIEW + all-clients MANAGE still denies manage for that client), contradicting the 'all-clients' semantics the fallback comment describes. The PR's tests never delete a per-client permission and then rely on a type-level grant, so this isn't covered.

`ClientPermissionsV2` throws raw `UnsupportedOperationException` from methods still declared on the shared `ClientPermissionEvaluator`/`ClientPermissionManagement` interfaces (`setPermissionsEnabled`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, `canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `managePermission`, etc.), while the `ClientRemovedEvent` listener (touched by this PR) still calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` on every client removal, and token-exchange and the V1 permission REST endpoints also call into this surface — so any V2-mode caller reaching these methods gets an unhandled 500 instead of graceful behavior; in particular, if `management()` dispatches to the V2 evaluator, deleting a client throws (or cleanup is silently skipped if the provider-event manager swallows listener exceptions).

V2 provides no replacement cleanup for per-client resources/policies when a client is removed: the only cleanup is the V1-flag-gated `ClientRemovedEvent` listener, which works solely because V1 happens to delete resources by the same name (`client.getId()`) in the same resource server — a fragile cross-version coupling. If V2 is ever enabled without the V1 feature flag, client/role/group removal leaves orphaned resources and policies accumulating in the `permission` client's resource server; the callers need to be gated/replaced or the listener made to call a V2-aware no-op-safe cleanup, and the assumption that the V2 feature formally depends on the V1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` feature needs explicit verification.

`hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` is not side-effect free: it may create the type-level resource as a side effect of a read-only permission check, whereas the type-level `hasPermission(String)` overload correctly avoids the resource-creating `getResourceTypeResource` call (same pattern as the merged users code, but worth knowing the check is not side-effect free).

ClientRemovedEvent cleanup listener in AdminPermissions calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), but ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException; since the listener now runs only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled (exactly when the V2 evaluator is active), every client deletion under the feature either fails/rolls back or silently skips cleanup, leaving orphaned per-client permission resources
With the feature disabled, the ClientRemovedEvent listener no longer performs V1 cleanup of legacy permission resources created before the feature was turned off

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException with no guard at the token-exchange call site, so cross-client token exchange requests fail with an unhandled 500 instead of an allow/deny decision when token-exchange and the admin-permissions feature are both enabled

Other V1-era stubs in ClientPermissionsV2 (isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission, etc.) also throw UnsupportedOperationException; if any legacy REST path (e.g., the old /clients/{id}/management/permissions endpoints) still routes to them under V2, those endpoints will 500 — needs confirmation these paths are dead in the truncated part of the diff

canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 dropped the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin-role bypass that V1 granted (and that V2 keeps for canManage/canView/canConfigure/canManageClientScopes), so a user holding the manage-clients realm admin role is denied role-mapping operations unless a separate explicit MAP_ROLES permission exists — a silent breaking behavior change vs V1 if intentional

All-clients MANAGE does not imply view/list of client scopes: canViewClientScopes/requireViewClientScopes delegate to canView() which checks only all-clients VIEW, so a MANAGE-only grantee can create/update/delete client scopes but gets 403 when listing or viewing them — inconsistent permission lattice producing mutate-but-cannot-read behavior
Dead code: the AccessToken-based evaluation context in ClientPermissionsV2 is only used by the throwing canExchangeTo, and the TOKEN_EXCHANGE import is unused — both should be deleted

`getClientsWithPermission` performs an unbounded scan of every Clients-type resource with one full policy evaluation per resource (N+1 pattern): `hasGrantedPermission` runs a complete authz policy engine pass plus `realmResourceServer()` and `getScopes()` lookups for each resource, with no limit, early exit, or caching of results, even when the caller only needs a single page (`first`/`max`) of results — latency scales with permission count, not result count

No memoization of policy evaluation results: `canView(client)` triggers up to 4 full policy evaluations for one logical answer (each repeating `findByName` + type-resource fallback + `findByResource` + engine run), `canView(ClientScopeModel)` evaluates twice via `hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE)` even though a single evaluation returns all granted scopes, and the base-class `getAccess(client)` re-evaluates `canManage(client)` roughly 3 times within a single request

Client-removal cleanup on `ClientRemovedEvent` in `AdminPermissions` calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException` when V2 is active, so nothing deletes the removed client's Clients-type resource and its policies — orphaned resources accumulate without bound as clients are deleted and permanently compound the unbounded scan in `getClientsWithPermission`
If the `UnsupportedOperationException` from `setPermissionsEnabled` instead propagates in-transaction, client deletion fails outright (potential P0) — this needs verification

Common-path `hasPermission(client, scope)` for a client without a per-client resource costs 3 store round trips: a `findByName` miss, then `getResourceTypeResource`, then `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` which materializes the full list of policies attached to the type resource just to test existence — a denied `canView(client)` costs ~12 store calls through multiplication

`getResourceTypeResource` may get-or-create the type resource on this read path, which would permanently convert the type-level `hasPermission(String)` fast-miss into a full evaluation for all subsequent checks in that realm — worth confirming

Client-removal event listener calls setPermissionsEnabled, which the new ClientPermissionsV2 implementation throws UnsupportedOperationException on: in a V2-enabled realm, DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} fires ClientRemovedEvent and the listener throws, causing a 500 and failed deletion; conversely, if the version-less feature check is false under V2, the listener is skipped entirely leaving V2 with no removal cleanup and orphaning 'Clients' resources for every deleted client

Twelve inherited evaluator methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) now throw UnsupportedOperationException with no visible caller updates, so the admin REST management-permissions endpoints and the token-exchange flow will surface raw 500s instead of proper 403/400 or 'not supported in V2' errors

All-clients grants are silently ignored for any client that has a per-client resource: the fallback to the type-level 'Clients' resource in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) only runs when resourceStore.findByName(...) returns null, so once a per-client permission exists for client X, canManage/canConfigure/canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles never consult the all-clients grant, producing false denials that contradict the documented contract (e.g., manage-all-clients granted to helpdesk plus one narrow per-client permission stops manage-all from working for that client)

V2 silently drops the manage-clients admin-role fallback for role-mapping checks: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 check only the FGAP permission with no root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) fallback (unlike canManage/canView in the same class), so an admin holding manage-clients in a V2 realm can create/update/delete clients but gets 403 on scope-mappings and composite-role endpoints

getClientsWithPermission can return the literal type-resource name 'Clients' in the granted-id set: resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients") also returns the type-level resource itself, and with an all-clients grant the string 'Clients' is added to a set consumers treat as client ids, causing callers using it as a whitelist to produce empty/incorrect listings instead of 'all clients'

The ClientRemovedEvent handler in AdminPermissions (gated to run when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled) calls management().clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which now dispatches to ClientPermissionsV2's implementation that throws UnsupportedOperationException — breaking client deletion cleanup: either the exception propagates through ProviderEventManager.publish causing a 500 on every client deletion, or it is swallowed and per-client resources plus their attached policies are orphaned in the authz store, leaking deleted client IDs into getClientsWithPermission() results

ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles omit the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin-role fallback that V1 and the sibling V2 methods (canManage, canView, canManageClientScopes) all have, so admins holding the manage-clients role get 403 on role-mapping operations; master-realm admins are permanently denied because hasPermission() unconditionally returns false for them, and the new tests only cover the granted-permission path so the regression is invisible to test coverage

ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException, so token exchange would hard-fail with an HTTP 500 under V2 instead of a controlled allow/deny; the port is visibly unfinished, evidenced by the dead getEvaluationContext helper, the unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import, and the unused logger

The rest of the V1 management surface that now throws in V2 (isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission, etc.) would surface as 500s to any surviving callers such as legacy REST endpoints or export/import tooling — reachability should be confirmed or these methods should return a controlled error/no-op

No test for the client-removal cleanup path: the PR makes ClientPermissionsV2.isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled throw UnsupportedOperationException while the modified ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions calls setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), so deleting a client with a per-client permission resource while the feature is enabled either 500s on every client deletion or silently skips V2 cleanup, orphaning per-client authorization resources that getClientsWithPermission() keeps enumerating and evaluating on every list call

MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope added to AdminPermissionsSchema has zero test coverage: no test grants it or exercises any endpoint gated by canMapClientScopeRoles, so if canMapClientScopeRoles checks the wrong scope constant or the endpoint it guards never consults it, the bug ships silently as an over-grant or under-grant

In testManageOnlyOneClient, the pre-grant 'can't remove default client scope' denial assertion is masked by an earlier failing call: clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) itself requires view permission and throws ForbiddenException before removeDefaultClientScope(...) is ever invoked, so the assertion is satisfied by the wrong operation and the test would pass even if removeDefaultClientScope had no permission check at all

No deny-path coverage for the new Clients resource type: (a) nothing verifies that a permission whose user policy targets a different user leaves the caller denied (if user policies matched everyone the suite would still pass), (b) Logic.NEGATIVE permissions are never exercised for Clients unlike Users, and (c) the hasPermission fallback that only consults the all-clients type resource when no per-client resource exists is untested, so a per-client resource with zero attached policies silently shadows an all-clients grant

AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient's by-clientId fallback is untested: every client permission test passes the internal ID (myclient.getId()), and no test creates a client permission referencing the client by its clientId string or covers the not-found path with a bogus id/clientId, so a wrong lookup or name normalization bug would ship untested

testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient over-grants scopes (MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, and CONFIGURE in a single permission, plus both a Users MAP_ROLES and a Clients MAP_ROLES for the role-mapping call), so it cannot detect wrong-scope gating: if addComposites erroneously checked MAP_ROLES instead of MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, or client-level role mapping checked only one of the two MAP_ROLES grants, the test would still pass

Client deletion breaks under the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature flag: AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management().clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every ClientRemovedEvent, but ClientPermissionsV2 overrides setPermissionsEnabled to throw UnsupportedOperationException, so with the feature enabled (and MgmtPermissionsV2 selected by management()) every client delete would throw and fail; the guard condition also appears inverted, enabling the listener exactly when V2 is active instead of keeping the legacy V1 cleanup out of the V2 path

ClientPermissionsV2 overrides framework-callback contract methods (setPermissionsEnabled, isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, mapRoles*Permission, canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission) to throw UnsupportedOperationException, which is a Liskov violation; these methods are reachable from existing admin REST endpoints (client management-permissions API, token-exchange evaluation) and would surface as 500s rather than graceful 404/403

hasPermission(ClientModel, String) in ClientPermissionsV2 uses either-or resource resolution: it evaluates the per-client resource and only falls back to the type-level 'Clients' resource if that is null, so all-clients/type-level grants are silently dropped whenever a per-client resource exists (created by any per-client permission for any scope), breaking FGAP's union semantics of mixing realm-wide grants with per-client exceptions

V2 map-roles evaluators (canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, canMapClientScopeRoles) are permission-only with no classic admin-role fallback (root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)) and no canManage implication, unlike all other V2 client evaluators which retain the fallback, so an admin holding the classic MANAGE_CLIENTS role could be denied role mapping in a realm with the feature enabled and no client permissions configured

Dead code copied from V1 in ClientPermissionsV2: the private getEvaluationContext(ClientModel, AccessToken) is never called (a remnant of V1's canExchangeTo, which V2 overrides to throw), the logger field is never used, and the TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import plus ClientModelIdentity/DefaultEvaluationContext/EvaluationContext/AccessToken imports exist only to serve the dead method

Triplicated permission-evaluation/scope-matching logic in ClientPermissionsV2: hasPermission(ClientModel, String), hasPermission(String), and hasGrantedPermission(Resource, String) each re-implement the same build-ResourcePermission/evaluate/match-scope loop with a subtle variation (Arrays.asList(scope).contains(s) vs scope.equals(s)), plus duplicated isAdminSameRealm()/realmResourceServer()/null-server preambles, and canManageClientScopes() re-implements canManage() inline instead of delegating, creating a divergence risk for security-critical authorization logic

ClientPermissionEvaluator javadoc for requireView() and requireViewClientScopes() incorrectly states boolean-return semantics ('Returns true if canView() returns true') for void methods that throw ForbiddenException on denial, a copy-paste error that misleads implementers and callers about control flow

getClientsWithPermission in ClientPermissionsV2 can return a bogus 'Clients' entry: it iterates resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and adds each resource's name to the granted set, but the type-level resource (named 'Clients') also carries that type, so 'Clients' is added whenever the all-clients permission grants the scope, violating the method's contract of returning client IDs

ClientPermissionsV2 overrides (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) throw UnsupportedOperationException, but live callers still invoke them: the ClientRemovedEvent branch of AdminPermissions.registerListener calls management().clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false) on every client deletion, so deletion either fails outright or cleanup silently never runs and per-client resources/policies for deleted clients accumulate forever; the /clients/{id}/management/permissions REST resource also calls the throwing methods directly, producing 500s for API/console consumers

Token exchange is broken in V2: canExchangeTo unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException and the V2 CLIENTS resource type in AdminPermissionsSchema has no token-exchange scope, so any cross-client token exchange under ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ returns HTTP 500 instead of an allow/deny decision; the leftover unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE import and dead getEvaluationContext helper indicate this was left half-finished

V2 drops the admin-role fallback in canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles (unlike canManage/canView/canConfigure which retain the hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_CLIENTS) check), so in V2 mode an admin holding the standard manage-clients role gets 403 on mapping client roles to users, adding composites, and client-scope role mappings — a regression for role-based admins

PermissionClientTest creates a user policy with the identical name 'Only My Admin User Policy' in all five test methods, but @AfterEach removes only scope permissions and not user policies (those are deferred to realm.cleanup() at class teardown), so the second and subsequent test methods fail with 409 Conflict at createUserPolicy, causing deterministic order-dependent CI breakage

getClientsWithPermission adds resource.getName() for every granted resource found by type, including the type-level 'all clients' resource itself named 'Clients', so the returned set of client IDs can contain the bogus literal string 'Clients' (plus IDs of never-cleaned deleted clients), yielding null/garbage lookups for callers; the loop should skip the type resource

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. adjudication_records.issue_text: `hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` is not side-effect free: it may create the type-level resource as a side effect of a read-only permission check, whereas the type-level `hasPermission(String)` overload correctly avoids the resource-creating `getResourceTypeResource` call (same pattern as the merged users code, but worth knowing the check is not side-effect free).

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, when a per-client resource is missing it falls back to `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)` (new file `ClientPermissionsV2.java`). By name and by the surrounding schema changes adding resource-type handling (`AdminPermissionsSchema` has `getOrCreateResource(...)` and now includes `CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE`), this call plausibly creates the type-level resource during what is otherwise a permission-check/read path. By contrast, the overload `hasPermission(String scope)` uses `resourceStore.findByName(...)` and returns `false` if the type resource is absent, avoiding any potential creation. This side-effect difference is grounded in the diff; whether it is undesirable is design/architecture rather than a clear functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientRemovedEvent cleanup listener in AdminPermissions calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), but ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException; since the listener now runs only when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled (exactly when the V2 evaluator is active), every client deletion under the feature either fails/rolls back or silently skips cleanup, leaving orphaned per-client permission resources

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener, the cleanup logic for ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent is now executed only when Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled, and it calls management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). In this diff, MgmtPermissionsV2 (the V2 permissions implementation for the feature) overrides clients() to return ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean) unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, when the feature is enabled and the V2 implementation is used, handling a ClientRemovedEvent will trigger an exception instead of performing cleanup, potentially breaking client deletion processing and/or leaving authz resources/policies uncleaned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: With the feature disabled, the ClientRemovedEvent listener no longer performs V1 cleanup of legacy permission resources created before the feature was turned off

adjudication.rationale: The diff wraps the entire ProviderEventListener cleanup logic in `if (Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)) { ... }` (services/.../AdminPermissions.java). Previously, `ClientRemovedEvent` (and role/group removals) always triggered `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` regardless of the feature flag. After this change, when the feature is disabled, no cleanup/disable call runs for `ClientRemovedEvent`, so any pre-existing permission artifacts would not be cleaned by this listener. Whether this is a true defect vs intended behavior is not provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo unconditionally throws UnsupportedOperationException with no guard at the token-exchange call site, so cross-client token exchange requests fail with an unhandled 500 instead of an allow/deny decision when token-exchange and the admin-permissions feature are both enabled

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo(...)` (and related permission methods) unconditionally throwing `UnsupportedOperationException` in the new `ClientPermissionsV2` class. However, the finding’s core claim—that there is “no guard at the token-exchange call site” and that this leads to “unhandled 500” during cross-client token exchange when features are enabled—cannot be verified from this diff because no token-exchange endpoint/call-site changes are included here. From the diff alone, we can’t confirm that these methods are invoked in that scenario or that the exception propagates as a 500 rather than being handled elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Other V1-era stubs in ClientPermissionsV2 (isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission, etc.) also throw UnsupportedOperationException; if any legacy REST path (e.g., the old /clients/{id}/management/permissions endpoints) still routes to them under V2, those endpoints will 500 — needs confirmation these paths are dead in the truncated part of the diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces ClientPermissionsV2 which overrides multiple inherited methods (e.g., isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission/configurePermission/viewPermission, mapRoles*Permission) to throw UnsupportedOperationException. MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() is also changed to return this ClientPermissionsV2, so any code path that still invokes these legacy-style methods under V2 would now fail at runtime. However, from this diff alone we cannot verify whether the legacy REST endpoints (or other call sites) are still reachable/routed to these methods in V2 mode, so the finding is a valid, specific concern but not a provable defect from the shown changes alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 dropped the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin-role bypass that V1 granted (and that V2 keeps for canManage/canView/canConfigure/canManageClientScopes), so a user holding the manage-clients realm admin role is denied role-mapping operations unless a separate explicit MAP_ROLES permission exists — a silent breaking behavior change vs V1 if intentional

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows ClientPermissionsV2 overrides canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles to only check hasPermission(client, <scope>) without an AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS bypass. However, the finding’s core claim that this is a breaking change “vs V1” (i.e., that V1 granted a MANAGE_CLIENTS bypass for these operations) is not verifiable from this diff because the V1 implementation (ClientPermissions) is not shown. Additionally, the newly added Javadocs in ClientPermissionEvaluator for these methods describe permission-based checks for V2 and do not state that MANAGE_CLIENTS should imply MAP_ROLES* access, so the V2 implementation is consistent with the contract presented in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: All-clients MANAGE does not imply view/list of client scopes: canViewClientScopes/requireViewClientScopes delegate to canView() which checks only all-clients VIEW, so a MANAGE-only grantee can create/update/delete client scopes but gets 403 when listing or viewing them — inconsistent permission lattice producing mutate-but-cannot-read behavior

adjudication.rationale: In the new V2 permission model, global client-scope viewing/listing appears to hinge on `canView()` rather than `MANAGE`. `ClientPermissionsV2.canView()` only returns true for default admin roles (`canViewClientDefault()`) or an all-clients `VIEW` permission (`hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`), and does not consider an all-clients `MANAGE` permission. At the same time, `ClientPermissionsV2.canManageClientScopes()` explicitly allows all-clients `MANAGE` (`hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`), and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` treats `MANAGE` as sufficient (`hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE)`). This mismatch supports the finding’s “mutate-but-cannot-read” scenario for client scopes when only all-clients MANAGE is granted, assuming (as the interface Javadoc states) `canViewClientScopes()` delegates to `canView()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead code: the AccessToken-based evaluation context in ClientPermissionsV2 is only used by the throwing canExchangeTo, and the TOKEN_EXCHANGE import is unused — both should be deleted

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, the static import `import static org.keycloak.services.resources.admin.permissions.AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE;` is not referenced anywhere in the new file, so it’s an unused import. Also, the private method `getEvaluationContext(ClientModel authorizedClient, AccessToken token)` is not called anywhere in `ClientPermissionsV2` (all token-exchange related overrides like `canExchangeTo`/`exchangeToPermission` throw `UnsupportedOperationException`), so it is dead code in this diff. This is a maintainability/cleanup issue, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `getClientsWithPermission` performs an unbounded scan of every Clients-type resource with one full policy evaluation per resource (N+1 pattern): `hasGrantedPermission` runs a complete authz policy engine pass plus `realmResourceServer()` and `getScopes()` lookups for each resource, with no limit, early exit, or caching of results, even when the caller only needs a single page (`first`/`max`) of results — latency scales with permission count, not result count

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission`, the method iterates over **all** resources of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and, for each resource, calls `hasGrantedPermission(resource, scope)`, which performs `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...))` (full policy evaluation) and also re-fetches `root.realmResourceServer()` and `resource.getScopes()` per resource. There is no pagination (`first`/`max`), no early-exit, and no caching, so latency scales with the total number of client resources/policies rather than the amount of results needed. This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No memoization of policy evaluation results: `canView(client)` triggers up to 4 full policy evaluations for one logical answer (each repeating `findByName` + type-resource fallback + `findByResource` + engine run), `canView(ClientScopeModel)` evaluates twice via `hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE)` even though a single evaluation returns all granted scopes, and the base-class `getAccess(client)` re-evaluates `canManage(client)` roughly 3 times within a single request

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2`, several permission checks can trigger multiple independent policy evaluations because `hasPermission(...)` both looks up resources (`resourceStore.findByName(...)` with a fallback to the type resource) and then runs `root.evaluatePermission(...)` each time. For example, `canView(ClientModel)` calls `canView()` (which may call `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)`) and may also call `canConfigure(client)` (which may call `canManage(client)` -> `hasPermission(client, MANAGE)` and then `hasPermission(client, CONFIGURE)`), and then may call `hasPermission(client, VIEW)` as a fallback—so multiple full evaluations are possible for a single logical answer. Also, `canView(ClientScopeModel)` does `hasPermission(VIEW) || hasPermission(MANAGE)`, which is two evaluations even though one evaluation returns all granted scopes. This is a concrete, diff-grounded efficiency/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect. The part about base-class `getAccess(client)` re-evaluating `canManage(client)` cannot be verified from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-removal cleanup on `ClientRemovedEvent` in `AdminPermissions` calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)`, which throws `UnsupportedOperationException` when V2 is active, so nothing deletes the removed client's Clients-type resource and its policies — orphaned resources accumulate without bound as clients are deleted and permanently compound the unbounded scan in `getClientsWithPermission`

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), ClientRemovedEvent still triggers management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false) when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled. This diff adds MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returning ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) explicitly throws UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, under V2/feature-enabled execution, client-removal cleanup will throw at runtime instead of performing any cleanup logic, which can plausibly leave authz artifacts (e.g., CLIENTS-type resources) behind and worsen the resourceStore.findByType(...) scan used by ClientPermissionsV2.getClientsWithPermission().

adjudication_records.issue_text: If the `UnsupportedOperationException` from `setPermissionsEnabled` instead propagates in-transaction, client deletion fails outright (potential P0) — this needs verification

adjudication.rationale: The listener in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` now runs on client removal events when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled and calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. In V2, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returns `ClientPermissionsV2`, where `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel client, boolean enable)` is overridden to `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")`. This means a `ClientRemovedEvent` can trigger an exception during deletion handling, plausibly aborting the in-transaction client removal.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Common-path `hasPermission(client, scope)` for a client without a per-client resource costs 3 store round trips: a `findByName` miss, then `getResourceTypeResource`, then `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()` which materializes the full list of policies attached to the type resource just to test existence — a denied `canView(client)` costs ~12 store calls through multiplication

adjudication.rationale: In the new `ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel, String)` method, when a per-client resource is missing it first calls `resourceStore.findByName(...)` (miss), then loads the type resource via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`, and then calls `authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()`. That last check requires fetching the policies collection (potentially materializing all attached policies) just to test existence. This is a real, diff-grounded performance concern on common deny paths (e.g., `canView(client)` calling `hasPermission(client, VIEW)`), though the exact “~12 store calls” multiplier is an estimate not provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `getResourceTypeResource` may get-or-create the type resource on this read path, which would permanently convert the type-level `hasPermission(String)` fast-miss into a full evaluation for all subsequent checks in that realm — worth confirming

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, when the per-client `Resource` is missing it calls `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)` on a permission-check/read path. If `getResourceTypeResource` is a get-or-create (as its name suggests and consistent with `AdminPermissionsSchema` having get-or-create resource logic), this would persist the type-level resource even when no type-level policies exist (note the subsequent `findByResource(...).isEmpty()` check happens *after* the call). That could change later behavior of `hasPermission(String)` (which fast-misses when `resourceStore.findByName(...)` returns null) into always doing an evaluation once the resource exists, impacting performance/side effects. The diff doesn’t show `getResourceTypeResource`’s implementation, so it’s a confirm-the-contract concern rather than a proven bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Client-removal event listener calls setPermissionsEnabled, which the new ClientPermissionsV2 implementation throws UnsupportedOperationException on: in a V2-enabled realm, DELETE /admin/realms/{realm}/clients/{id} fires ClientRemovedEvent and the listener throws, causing a 500 and failed deletion; conversely, if the version-less feature check is false under V2, the listener is skipped entirely leaving V2 with no removal cleanup and orphaning 'Clients' resources for every deleted client

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissions.registerListener(), when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled it handles ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent by calling management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false). The diff introduces MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() returning ClientPermissionsV2, and ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(...) explicitly throws UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). If management(...) resolves to the V2 permission implementation under the same feature flag, a client deletion event will trigger this call path and raise an exception during event handling, breaking the removal cleanup flow and potentially failing the delete operation and/or leaving authz artifacts behind.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Twelve inherited evaluator methods in ClientPermissionsV2 (canExchangeTo, exchangeToPermission, mapRolesPermission, mapRolesClientScopePermission, mapRolesCompositePermission, managePermission, configurePermission, viewPermission, isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) now throw UnsupportedOperationException with no visible caller updates, so the admin REST management-permissions endpoints and the token-exchange flow will surface raw 500s instead of proper 403/400 or 'not supported in V2' errors

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that ClientPermissionsV2 overrides multiple inherited methods (e.g., canExchangeTo, *Permission(...), isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions) to throw UnsupportedOperationException (new file ClientPermissionsV2.java). MgmtPermissionsV2.clients() is also changed to return ClientPermissionsV2, so any code path that still calls these methods when V2 is active would now fail at runtime rather than returning a structured “not supported”/403 response. However, the claim that “admin REST management-permissions endpoints and token-exchange flow will surface raw 500s” is not directly verifiable from this diff alone because no call sites/endpoints are shown invoking these methods under V2; it’s a valid risk/robustness concern but not a provable defect from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: All-clients grants are silently ignored for any client that has a per-client resource: the fallback to the type-level 'Clients' resource in hasPermission(ClientModel, String) only runs when resourceStore.findByName(...) returns null, so once a per-client permission exists for client X, canManage/canConfigure/canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles never consult the all-clients grant, producing false denials that contradict the documented contract (e.g., manage-all-clients granted to helpdesk plus one narrow per-client permission stops manage-all from working for that client)

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code first looks up a per-client resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`. Only if that lookup returns `null` does it fall back to evaluating the type-level "all-clients" resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(..., CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`). When a per-client resource exists, it evaluates permissions solely against that per-client resource (`new ResourcePermission(resource, resource.getScopes(), server)`) and never evaluates the type-level `Clients` resource policies. Therefore, an admin who has a type-level grant (e.g., MANAGE on all clients) can be denied for a specific client that happens to have its own resource, matching the finding's described false-denial scenario and contradicting the interface Javadoc claims that V2 also honors permissions for all clients.

adjudication_records.issue_text: V2 silently drops the manage-clients admin-role fallback for role-mapping checks: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles in ClientPermissionsV2 check only the FGAP permission with no root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS) fallback (unlike canManage/canView in the same class), so an admin holding manage-clients in a V2 realm can create/update/delete clients but gets 403 on scope-mappings and composite-role endpoints

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, `canMapRoles(ClientModel)`, `canMapCompositeRoles(ClientModel)`, and `canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` return only `hasPermission(client, ...)` (FGAP scope evaluation) and do not include any `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)` (or other admin-role) fallback, unlike `canManage(ClientModel)` / `canManageClientScopes()` which explicitly allow `MANAGE_CLIENTS`. As written, a caller with the legacy `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin role but without the new FGAP permissions would be allowed by `canManage(...)` yet denied by these map-roles checks, causing 403s on endpoints guarded by these methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getClientsWithPermission can return the literal type-resource name 'Clients' in the granted-id set: resourceStore.findByType(server, "Clients") also returns the type-level resource itself, and with an all-clients grant the string 'Clients' is added to a set consumers treat as client ids, causing callers using it as a whitelist to produce empty/incorrect listings instead of 'all clients'

The ClientRemovedEvent handler in AdminPermissions (gated to run when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled) calls management().clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), which now dispatches to ClientPermissionsV2's implementation that throws UnsupportedOperationException — breaking client deletion cleanup: either the exception propagates through ProviderEventManager.publish causing a 500 on every client deletion, or it is swallowed and per-client resources plus their attached policies are orphaned in the authz store, leaking deleted client IDs into getClientsWithPermission() results

adjudication.rationale: In `AdminPermissions.registerListener`, when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled it handles `ClientRemovedEvent` by calling `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. This diff adds `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` returning a `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException` ("Not supported in V2"). Therefore, under the feature gate, a client deletion event can now trigger an exception during cleanup instead of disabling/removing permissions, which risks breaking client removal processing and/or leaving authz artifacts uncleared.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles, and canMapClientScopeRoles omit the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin-role fallback that V1 and the sibling V2 methods (canManage, canView, canManageClientScopes) all have, so admins holding the manage-clients role get 403 on role-mapping operations; master-realm admins are permanently denied because hasPermission() unconditionally returns false for them, and the new tests only cover the granted-permission path so the regression is invisible to test coverage

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, ClientPermissionsV2.canMapRoles/canMapCompositeRoles/canMapClientScopeRoles intentionally delegate only to hasPermission(client, …) and do not include an AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS fallback. The updated ClientPermissionEvaluator Javadocs for these methods also describe only scope-permission based checks (and for V2, only “permission for all clients”), not “MANAGE_CLIENTS implies map-roles”, so the claim that this omission is a regression relative to the intended contract is not supported by what’s shown. While hasPermission() does return false when !root.isAdminSameRealm(), the finding’s assertion that this permanently/incorrectly denies master-realm admins cannot be verified from the diff alone (it may be intended behavior in V2).

adjudication_records.issue_text: ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo and exchangeToPermission throw UnsupportedOperationException, so token exchange would hard-fail with an HTTP 500 under V2 instead of a controlled allow/deny; the port is visibly unfinished, evidenced by the dead getEvaluationContext helper, the unused TOKEN_EXCHANGE static import, and the unused logger

The rest of the V1 management surface that now throws in V2 (isPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, managePermission, etc.) would surface as 500s to any surviving callers such as legacy REST endpoints or export/import tooling — reachability should be confirmed or these methods should return a controlled error/no-op

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces `ClientPermissionsV2` and overrides a large part of the prior management API surface to throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported in V2")` (e.g., `isPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, and several `*Permission(...)` methods). Additionally, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns this implementation, so any code path that still calls these methods when running in V2 would crash at runtime. The finding’s concern about potential 500s is plausible, but the diff alone does not prove these methods are reachable by legacy endpoints/tooling; it does show the risk and that reachability should be checked or handled more gracefully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No test for the client-removal cleanup path: the PR makes ClientPermissionsV2.isPermissionsEnabled/setPermissionsEnabled throw UnsupportedOperationException while the modified ClientRemovedEvent listener in AdminPermissions calls setPermissionsEnabled(client, false), so deleting a client with a per-client permission resource while the feature is enabled either 500s on every client deletion or silently skips V2 cleanup, orphaning per-client authorization resources that getClientsWithPermission() keeps enumerating and evaluating on every list call

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a V2 implementation where `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException` (and also `isPermissionsEnabled`), but the modified `AdminPermissions.registerListener` now unconditionally calls `management(session, realm).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)` on `ClientModel.ClientRemovedEvent` whenever `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. If `management(...).clients()` resolves to the V2 implementation (as `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returns `new ClientPermissionsV2(...)`), client deletion will trigger an exception during the removal event handling, breaking the cleanup path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE scope added to AdminPermissionsSchema has zero test coverage: no test grants it or exercises any endpoint gated by canMapClientScopeRoles, so if canMapClientScopeRoles checks the wrong scope constant or the endpoint it guards never consults it, the bug ships silently as an over-grant or under-grant

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` to `AdminPermissionsSchema` and wires it into the new `CLIENTS` resource type scopes set, and `ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` checks exactly this scope (`hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`). In the added/modified tests, `PermissionClientTest` grants `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` (and `CONFIGURE`) but never grants `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE`, nor is there any test that exercises behavior specifically requiring that scope. From the diff alone, this is a concrete missing-test gap for newly introduced permission logic (though whether an endpoint actually consults `canMapClientScopeRoles` is not shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: In testManageOnlyOneClient, the pre-grant 'can't remove default client scope' denial assertion is masked by an earlier failing call: clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1) itself requires view permission and throws ForbiddenException before removeDefaultClientScope(...) is ever invoked, so the assertion is satisfied by the wrong operation and the test would pass even if removeDefaultClientScope had no permission check at all

adjudication.rationale: In PermissionClientTest.testManageOnlyOneClient the pre-grant denial block does `clientResource.getDefaultClientScopes().get(1)` and then `removeDefaultClientScope(...)` inside a single try/catch that accepts any ForbiddenException. Given the same test already expects `clientResource.toRepresentation()` to be forbidden pre-grant, it is plausible that `getDefaultClientScopes()` is also forbidden pre-grant, meaning the exception could be thrown before `removeDefaultClientScope(...)` is actually executed. The test therefore may not specifically assert that `removeDefaultClientScope` is permission-checked, and could pass even if only listing default scopes is forbidden. This is a test robustness issue grounded in the diff, not a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No deny-path coverage for the new Clients resource type: (a) nothing verifies that a permission whose user policy targets a different user leaves the caller denied (if user policies matched everyone the suite would still pass), (b) Logic.NEGATIVE permissions are never exercised for Clients unlike Users, and (c) the hasPermission fallback that only consults the all-clients type resource when no per-client resource exists is untested, so a per-client resource with zero attached policies silently shadows an all-clients grant

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new Clients resource type/scopes (AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS, CONFIGURE, MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE) and nontrivial authorization logic in ClientPermissionsV2, including a fallback path in hasPermission(ClientModel,String) that only checks the all-clients type resource when the per-client resource is missing. The new tests in PermissionClientTest cover basic deny-before-grant and allow-after-grant for MANAGE/CONFIGURE/VIEW and mapping roles, but they do not include (a) a deny test where a permission exists but the policy targets a different user (all tests create policies for the same caller user), (b) any Logic.NEGATIVE permissions for Clients (negative is exercised for Users in UserResourceTypeEvaluationTest but not for Clients), or (c) a case where a per-client resource exists with zero attached policies to verify the fallback behavior (since hasPermission won’t fall back when resource != null). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a confirmed runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient's by-clientId fallback is untested: every client permission test passes the internal ID (myclient.getId()), and no test creates a client permission referencing the client by its clientId string or covers the not-found path with a bogus id/clientId, so a wrong lookup or name normalization bug would ship untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new lookup logic in `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveClient` that falls back from `getClientById(realm, id)` to `getClientByClientId(realm, id)` and returns null if neither is found. In the added/updated client permission tests (`PermissionClientTest`), permissions for a specific client are always created using the internal UUID (`myclient.getId()` / `realmClient.getId()`), e.g. `createPermission(client, myclient.getId(), clientsType, Set.of(MANAGE), ...)`, and no test creates a permission using the public `clientId` string nor exercises the null/not-found path. Therefore the fallback branch and its behavior are indeed untested by this diff, which is a concrete coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: hasPermission(ClientModel, String) in ClientPermissionsV2 uses either-or resource resolution: it evaluates the per-client resource and only falls back to the type-level 'Clients' resource if that is null, so all-clients/type-level grants are silently dropped whenever a per-client resource exists (created by any per-client permission for any scope), breaking FGAP's union semantics of mixing realm-wide grants with per-client exceptions

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope)`, the code looks up a per-client resource (`resourceStore.findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId())`) and evaluates permissions only on that resource when it exists. It falls back to the type-level/all-clients resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`) only when the per-client resource is `null`. This means if a per-client resource exists (e.g., created due to any per-client permission on any scope), any realm-wide/type-level grant for the same scope is not considered, so effective permissions are not the union of per-client and all-clients grants.
